- PCR-confirmed influenza infection — a confirmed case of influenza infection through a specific laboratory test
- index case-patient — the first person in a household to show symptoms of illness
- household compounds — the group of households included in the study
- intent-to-treat analysis — an analysis that includes all participants as assigned to their group, regardless of whether they completed the intervention
- design effect — a measure of how much the variability of a statistic increases due to the cluster sampling design
- intracluster correlation — a measure of how similar individuals within the same cluster are
- susceptible household members — individuals in the household who were at risk of getting the illness
- multivariable models — statistical models that consider multiple variables simultaneously
- confidence intervals — a range of values used to estimate the uncertainty around a statistic
- relative risk — a measure of the risk of an event occurring in an exposed group versus a non-exposed group
- interquartile range — the range between the first and third quartiles of a dataset
